questions.independent_solution: Actual complete figure is series C-R-L across the source, so the same I passes every element. For stated passive signs and e^(j omega t), U_R=RI is real positive/right, U_L=j*omegaL*I is up, U_C=I/(j*omegaC) is down. Current resonance imposes omegaL=1/(omegaC), making reactive voltage magnitudes equal, not each zero. Their sum vanishes and source U=U_R+U_L+U_C=U_R points right. Complete true set {a,c,e}, covering common current and every voltage direction. This is phasor relationship recognition; no claim of independent drawing skill.

option_checks.evidence: Single uninterrupted series path in the opened image has no branch; continuity gives equal C,R,L current phasorsI.
At nonzero driven current, U_L=j*omegaLI and U_C=-jI/(omegaC) are nonzero opposite phasors; cancellation of their sum does not make each vanish.
With positive R and rightwardI, U_R=RI points right. Resonant cancellation makes U=U_R and hence rightward as well.
Under e^(j omega t) and counterclockwise positive phase, inductance has+j reactance (up), capacitance-j (down); d swaps these signs.
U_L is+90 degrees/up and U_C is-90 degrees/down; omegaL=1/(omegaC) gives equal magnitudes.
KVL includes the resistor: U=U_R+U_L+U_C. Proposed U=U_L+U_C=0 omits nonzeroU_R and cannot represent the driven resistive series circuit.
